design: Within-subjects counterbalanced (AB/BA) across Co-Plan (treatment) and Baseline (control)

items.label: Mental Demand
items.prompt: How mentally demanding was the task?

items.label: Temporal Demand
items.prompt: How hurried or rushed was the pace of the task?

items.label: Performance
items.prompt: How successful were you in accomplishing what you were asked to do?

items.label: Effort
items.prompt: How hard did you have to work to accomplish your level of performance?

items.label: Frustration
items.prompt: How insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed were you?
I felt in control of the agent's direction throughout the task.
I could easily tell what the agent was planning and doing at every moment.
Handling the mid-task requirement change felt smooth and predictable.
I trusted the system not to overwrite or break parts of the document I already approved.
When the agent went off-track, recovering to a good state was effortless.
The agent paused for my input at the right moments without nagging me.

open_ended.prompt: What helped you most when steering the agent after the mid-task requirement change?
What caused the most friction or confusion in this interface?
Comparing both interfaces, which would you prefer for real high-stakes work and why?
